scores.evidence: decisions → runners, registry, access and GitOps → pilot in production → versioned templates → Wave 1 → 2 → 3.
scores.rationale: Clear substrate-up sequencing with explicit done-when gates and prerequisites (e.g., versioning templates before 50 depend on them, signed images before admission).

scores.evidence: Pilot service to production (weeks 6–12)... Why one service to production before many to dev
scores.rationale: A real pilot through prod with rollback drill precedes wide rollout, though Foundations comes first as a thin substrate phase with a test service commit-to-prod.

scores.evidence: Write down the decisions that are expensive to reverse: One repo or many... GitOps (Argo CD or Flux)... Leave easy-to-change choices... for later.
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed with some recommended defaults, but flip/revisit conditions are mostly absent.

scores.evidence: Size them for peak load... Version the templates before 50 services depend on them... One careless change to an unversioned template can break all 50 pipelines
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (foundations, templates, pilot) precede leaf services, and within phases shared work precedes per-service; critical services deliberately last with reasoning.

scores.evidence: secret scan (blocking from day one...)... software bill of materials → sign → push... Secrets manager, plus OIDC trust
scores.rationale: Security appears in foundations (OIDC, SSO, audit), pilot (scan, sign, SBOM), templates, migration criteria and enforcement, though Phase 0 security is light.

scores.evidence: Metrics, logs and tracing for both the services and the pipelines.
scores.rationale: Observability begins in Foundations and recurs (pipeline stats, dashboards), but Phase 0 baseline is only DORA measurement and later phases are thinner.

scores.evidence: Build once, deploy the same artifact everywhere... Build everything as infrastructure-as-code... Services pin a version
scores.rationale: Immutable artifacts, IaC, GitOps, pinned template versions and fresh runners thread reproducibility across phases.

scores.evidence: expand/contract... a rollback you've actually practiced... Run in audit mode first... time-limited exceptions
scores.rationale: Resilience (rollback drills, migration safety, template canary rollout, peak sizing, canary releases) appears in most phases from pilot onward.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so no N/A declaration.

scores.evidence: Add a developer portal only after the standard path is proven... Developer portal: after Wave 1, and never allowed to delay the main sequence.
scores.rationale: Deferred items (portal, PR environments, blocking, admission, removal of approvals) are explicit with 'Needs' pull-forward prerequisites.

note: Strong, well-sequenced CI/CD plan with concrete prerequisites and deferrals; weaker on flip conditions for decisions, Phase 0 observability, and never declaring the AI layer N/A.
